source.title: Rethinking embedding coupling in pre-trained language models
source.authors: Hyung Won Chung; Thibault Févry; Henry Tsai; Melvin Johnson; Sebastian Ruder

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream-task performance under changes to pre-training capacity, using task metrics rather than held-out cross-entropy scaling measurements.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, fit power laws, test extrapolation from small runs, or search for a compute-optimal parameter/token split. Its own downstream task results under capacity changes bear on V6. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests embedding decoupling and capacity allocation, not scaling laws. It cites Kaplan et al. (Appendix A.1) only to justify comparing models by fine-tuning parameter count. No pretraining loss is measured and no power law is fitted. The downstream gains come from enlarging an output embedding that is discarded before fine-tuning, or from reallocating parameters at roughly fixed fine-tuning size. Many rows compare the study's own method with its baseline. None measures downstream performance improving predictably with model scale or pretraining loss, so no version is tested; the Eout trend is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that larger output embeddings stop upper layers over-specializing to MLM, making representations more general and transferable across tasks and languages. They state that input embeddings can be safely reduced.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies embedding dimensions and Transformer capacity in masked-language-model pre-training and evaluates downstream task performance; it does not measure the original scaling-law loss curves, fit exponents, or optimize parameter/token allocations for compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream outcomes depend on how added pre-training capacity is allocated: increasing Eout improves the reported scores, while adding layers and dropping them before fine-tuning can perform worse; the English L = 24 setting also scores below L = 15.

fits_no_version.finding: Enlarging only the pre-training output embedding (Eout 128→768→3072, later discarded) raises downstream XTREME average 56.6→60.2→61.8 at fixed 100M fine-tuning parameters. English MNLI/SQuAD scores rise the same way. MLM accuracy also rises with Eout (59.0→60.7→62.3, Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pre-training-only capacity that is discarded before fine-tuning still improves downstream performance, tracking pre-training task accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: At similar parameter counts, how capacity is allocated changes downstream scores by several points. Reinvesting in depth beats width (66.2 vs 64.5), and Eout beats added-then-dropped layers (60.2 vs 58.0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream performance at fixed parameter count depends materially on capacity allocation (embedding vs layers, depth vs width).

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the downstream scores. The results concern a limited set of embedding and layer configurations and do not establish a general scale-to-performance relationship or measure pre-training loss.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2 and 3 compare embedding coupling and shape allocations but do not test scale-related downstream predictability as defined here. Table 8 reports MLM accuracy and embedding association measures, not held-out cross-entropy loss or downstream task performance. Probing and nearest-neighbor transfer results in Tables 9 and Figures 1-2 are not the downstream task-performance measure in V6.

untested.parts: All: no held-out loss curves or power-law fits.
All: no extrapolation from small runs.
Loss at fixed parameter count versus shape is not measured. Width vs depth comparisons (Table 6) use downstream scores only.
All: no other modalities or regimes.
Downstream predictability with model scale or pretraining loss: no fitted trend and no true scale sweep.
All: no exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Kaplan et al. is cited only to justify parameter count as an efficiency proxy. The authors call the English Table 13 results monotonic, yet L=24 scores below L=15 because of pruning. No uncertainty estimates are given; results are averaged over three fine-tuning runs.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pre-training loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law form and range.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their trends with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and architecture on loss at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities and training regimes such as repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer.

The study varies embedding and layer capacity and reports downstream task scores, but does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from held-out pre-training loss or establish a general scale-to-performance law.
Dependence of scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices, or bending away from power laws.

rows.subject: model with Eout = 128 (Ein = 128)
rows.operation_detail: Varied output embedding size while holding Ein and other model components fixed; evaluated on XTREME tasks.
rows.note: Reported as the average over the listed XTREME tasks.
rows.check: Starting point of a three-point Eout sweep. Pre-training-only capacity at a fixed 100M fine-tuning size is not model scale as V6 means it.

rows.subject: model with Eout = 3072 (Ein = 128)
rows.operation_detail: Varied output embedding size while holding Ein and other model components fixed; evaluated on XTREME tasks.

rows.check: Eout sweep with fine-tuned model size fixed; no scale-predictability measure.

rows.subject: model with Eout = 768 (Ein = 128)
rows.operation_detail: Compared output-embedding capacity with adding and then dropping Transformer layers during pre-training.
rows.note: The comparison models have similar pre-training and the same fine-tuning parameter counts.
rows.check: Compares two ways of adding pre-training capacity at equal parameters; this is a method comparison, not scale.

rows.subject: model with 11 additional layers during pre-training
rows.operation_detail: Added 11 Transformer layers for pre-training and dropped those upper layers before fine-tuning.
rows.note: The additional-layer strategy scores lower than the Eout = 768 comparison despite similar pre-training parameter counts.
rows.check: 'Reversed' is wrong: this is an allocation comparison at equal parameter count (193M vs 192M), not a scale effect.

rows.subject: baseline model with coupled embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Measured XTREME task performance for the coupled-embedding baseline.
rows.note: Baseline reference for the parameter-reinvestment comparisons.
rows.check: Baseline reference value only.

rows.subject: model with Ein = 128, Eout = 768
rows.operation_detail: Measured XTREME task performance with reduced input and enlarged output embedding dimensions.
rows.note: The paper includes this configuration as an ablation before reinvesting saved input-embedding parameters.
rows.check: Ablation that reduces fine-tuning parameters; it measures embedding allocation, not scaling.

rows.subject: model with input embedding parameters reinvested in hidden dimension
rows.operation_detail: Reduced Ein and reinvested saved input-embedding parameters by increasing hidden dimension H.
rows.note: The paper reports improved performance across all tasks for both reinvestment strategies.
rows.check: Study's own reinvestment method compared with its baseline; should not be scored against a scaling claim.

rows.subject: model with input embedding parameters reinvested in Transformer layers
rows.operation_detail: Reduced Ein and reinvested saved input-embedding parameters by increasing the number of Transformer layers.
rows.note: The paper reports the best score among the Table 6 settings.
rows.check: Study's own reinvestment method compared with its baseline; should not be scored against a scaling claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Increasing Eout in multilingual XTREME experiments and English BERTBase output-embedding experiments
reader_labels.reason: Downstream averages or task metrics improve as Eout grows in the reported comparisons (r1-r3, r16-r21).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reinvesting input-embedding parameters in Transformer hidden size or layer count
reader_labels.reason: Both reinvestment settings exceed the coupled baseline average, with the layer-count setting highest (r8-r9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Capacity added through extra Transformer layers, including the largest English layer setting
reader_labels.reason: Adding and then dropping layers scores below the Eout = 768 alternative, and the English L = 24 results are below L = 15 (r5, r25-r27).
